To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TAK-044 attenuates ischemia-reperfusion injury by inhibiting the activation of the hepatic stellate cell and Kupffer cell.

the endothelin receptor agonist, BQ-123, attenuates the ischemia-reperfusion-induced hepatocyte element alterations, whereas the endothelin receptor antagonists, bosentan and TAK-044, exacerbate the alterations, in the ischemic reperfused liver in canine model.

the endothelin receptor inhibitor TAK-044, administered before the ischemia period, attenuated the hepatic injury and hepatocyte element alterations induced by ischemic-reperfusion (I/R) in the canine liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) on hepatic injury after ischemia-reperfusion in Beagle dogs, and the mechanisms underlying these effects.
the effect of the endothelin (ET) receptor antagonist TAK 044 on hepatocyte alterations in ischemic-reperfusions in the dog liver.
the effects of TAK-044, an endothelin receptor antagonist, on hepatic microcirculatory disturbances in the ischemia/reperfusion model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of TAK-044 are not as good as those of the standard of care in terms of the prevention of ischemia-reperfusion injury.
the effects of the endothelin antagonist on liver injury and function in the setting of ischemia-reperfusion are still controversial.
the use of the endothelin antagonist TAK- 044 in the treatment of ischemic-reperfusional hepatic damage in Beagle dogs is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelin receptor blocker TAK-044 attenuates hepatic ischemia-reperfusion (IR) injury.
the endothelin (ET) program has an important function in the pathogenesis of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion damage.
the endothelin receptor antagonists (ETAs) have the potential to become effective agents for protecting the ischemic-repereduced liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the TGF-beta pathway to modulate the effects of the endothelin system in the liver.

endothelin receptor antagonists may represent a novel therapeutic approach to prevent ischemia/reperfusion injury of the liver.
